mainTopic: The sources and limits of the rule that relatives cannot testify: which relatives, which kinds of testimony and cases, how many generations (רב and רבי אלעזר), and in-law cases
overview: The גמרא finishes finding the sources for why relatives cannot be witnesses, all from the פסוק 'לא יומתו אבות על בנים ובנים לא יומתו על אבות'. The plural words teach that uncles, nephews, brothers and cousins are disqualified. רמי בר חמא tries to prove from logic that relatives also cannot pair up as witnesses about an outsider, but רבא knocks that proof down. The גמרא then learns it from the extra word 'ובנים'. Repeated words in the פסוק teach that the mother's relatives are included, and that a relative cannot testify even in his relative's favor. 'משפט אחד' extends all of this to money cases. Next, רב says his son cannot testify about רב's uncle (third generation with first). After several attempts to find this in the משנה, the גמרא concludes that רב agrees with רבי אלעזר on that point but disagrees with him about third with second. Each view is explained from the same פסוק. Finally, רב נחמן and עולא show that several in-law cases are already in the משנה when its list is read from the other relative's side. A new story about רב begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Summing up what we have found so far
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up what the plural 'אבות על בנים' has already taught: fathers (and their brothers) cannot testify about the children, and the children cannot testify about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source that fathers cannot testify about children, and children cannot testify about fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is summing up what it already learned from the פסוק. This sets the stage for the next questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'אבות' and 'בנים' in the plural, not 'a father for his son.' From that, the גמרא learned that the disqualification reaches beyond father and son. A father's brother and his nephew also cannot testify about each other, in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for this)
Fathers; here it includes the father's brothers too
Children; here it includes the brothers' children (nephews)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אבות לבנים' does not only mean a father and his own son. Because of the plural, it also covers an uncle (the father's brother) and his nephew.

phrases.english: We have found [a source for] fathers about children,
phrases.notes: This comes from the plural wording of the פסוק in דברים 24:16. It includes an uncle testifying about his brother's children.

phrases.english: and children about fathers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by summing up the earlier derivation from the plural 'אבות על בנים'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fathers (including a father's brothers) and children (including nephews) cannot testify about one another, in either direction.

steps.title: Brothers are disqualified all the more so
steps.stepSummary: Using a קל וחומר, the גמרא adds that the 'fathers' themselves, meaning brothers, certainly cannot testify about each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all the more so, the fathers (brothers) cannot testify about each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more group, brothers, using simple logic instead of a new פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an uncle cannot testify about his nephew, then two brothers cannot testify about each other either, because brothers are even more closely related than an uncle and a nephew. So no extra source is needed for brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a קל וחומר argument)

phrases.english: And all the more so, fathers about each other.
phrases.notes: 'Fathers' here means two brothers, who are the fathers of the children in the earlier case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 1 with a קל וחומר to include brothers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers cannot testify about each other, since they are closer relatives than an uncle and a nephew.

steps.title: Where do we learn that cousins are disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the children of one brother cannot testify about the children of the other brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Children about children, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: we have covered uncles, nephews and brothers, but what about cousins?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר from step 2 does not work for cousins, because cousins are more distant relatives than an uncle and a nephew. So the גמרא needs a separate source to disqualify them.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Children about children, from where do we [know it]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After covering fathers, children and brothers, the גמרא asks about the remaining case: cousins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the children of two brothers (cousins) cannot testify about each other.

steps.title: The extra plural 'בנים' teaches that cousins are disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תורה could have written 'על בן' in the singular. Writing 'בנים' in the plural teaches that even the brothers' children cannot testify about each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so (that cousins could testify), let the פסוק write: 'Fathers shall not be put to death for a son.' Why does it say 'children'? To teach that even children cannot testify about each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to an extra plural word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To teach that many 'fathers' (brothers) cannot testify about a child, the פסוק only needed 'אבות על בן.' Since it wrote 'בנים' in the plural as well, that extra plural must come to teach something new: the children of the brothers, the cousins, are also disqualified from testifying about each other.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your idea were true)
Let the פסוק write (it could have said it differently)
What is the meaning of / why

steps.whatToRemember: From the plural words of 'לא יומתו אבות על בנים': uncles and nephews are disqualified, brothers are disqualified by a קל וחומר, and cousins are disqualified because the תורה wrote 'בנים' and not 'בן'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the list of close relatives who are disqualified as witnesses, a basic rule in the laws of testimony.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write:
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: if cousins could testify about each other.

phrases.english: "Fathers shall not be put to death for a son"!
phrases.notes: The real פסוק says 'בנים'. The גמרא is imagining how it would read if it said only 'בן'.

phrases.english: What is [the meaning of] "children"?
That even children [cannot testify] about each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3 by learning from the extra plural word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural 'בנים', where 'בן' would have been enough, teaches that the children of brothers (cousins) cannot testify about each other.

steps.title: Can relatives testify together about someone else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that relatives cannot serve together as a pair of witnesses about an outside person.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found that the children of brothers cannot testify about each other. How do we know that they also cannot testify together as a pair about other people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts what it just learned and opens a new question: may two cousins team up as the two witnesses in someone else's case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now every case was about a relative testifying about his own relative. This new case is different: neither witness is related to the person on trial. The two witnesses are only related to each other. The פסוק from step 4 does not clearly cover this, so the גמרא needs a new source.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'to the world', meaning about other people

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. 'להדדי' means one relative testifies about the other. 'לעלמא' means the two relatives stand together as a pair of witnesses about an outsider.

phrases.english: We found that children cannot testify about each other;
children testifying together about the rest of the world, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He means two cousins acting as a pair of witnesses about some outside person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אשכחן בנים להדדי, בנים לעלמא מנלן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 4 and asks about a wider case it does not clearly cover.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that relatives may not join together as the two witnesses about an outside party.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: it is logic, based on how הזמה works
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says no פסוק is needed. Logic shows it: a זומם witness is punished only if his partner is also proven false, so his punishment would depend on his relative's testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: It is logical. A ברייתא teaches that witnesses are not punished as זוממין unless both of them are proven false. So if relatives could testify together about others, one false witness would end up being executed because of his relative's testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא answers the question. He uses a known rule about הזמה to show that relatives as a pair would really be testifying about each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses become זוממין only together. So whether witness A is punished depends on witness B being proven false too. If B is A's relative, B's testimony helps decide A's fate. That is the same as a relative testifying about a relative, which we already know is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Witnesses proven false by other witnesses who say 'you were with us elsewhere'
And if it would enter your mind (to say)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the reason the הלכה bans relatives from joining as a pair of witnesses. רבא's challenge in the next step tests this exact reason.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
It is logical reasoning,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
Witnesses do not become zomemim
unless both of them are proven zomemim.
And if it enters your mind
that children are valid to testify together about others,
it turns out that a zomem witness is executed
through the testimony of his brother.
phrases.notes: 'Brother' here just means his relative, who was proven false along with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רמי בר חמא: סברא הוא, כדתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No פסוק is needed. Since הזמה needs both witnesses, a pair of relatives would make one relative's punishment depend on the other's testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relatives may not serve together as witnesses about others, because הזמה would make each one's fate depend on the other.

steps.title: רבא challenges using the case of three brothers
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה where three brothers each testify with an outside witness. Their testimony is accepted, yet they count as one testimony for הזמה. So one brother would pay money because of his brother's testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: According to your reasoning, look at the משנה: three brothers, each joined by one outside witness, are counted as three separate testimonies, but as one testimony for הזמה. So a זומם witness ends up paying money because of his brother's testimony, and still the testimony is accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רמי בר חמא's logic. He shows a case in a משנה where one brother's punishment depends on another brother, and the testimony is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the three pairs of witnesses are judged together for הזמה. So no one pays unless all of them are proven false, and that includes his brothers. That is exactly the 'punished through his brother's testimony' problem רמי בר חמא described, yet the משנה accepts it. So his logic cannot be the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: But according to your own reasoning
Joins together (to make a pair of witnesses)
Counted as one testimony for the purpose of הזמה

steps.whatToRemember: רמי בר חמא says relatives cannot pair up, because one's punishment would depend on the other. רבא answers that the משנה of three brothers allows exactly that kind of dependence.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But according to your reasoning,
what about that which we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: בבא בתרא 56b, about witnesses who say a man held a field for three years.

phrases.english: Three brothers
and one outside witness joins with them,
phrases.notes: Each brother testifies about a different year, and the outsider is the second witness alongside each one.

phrases.english: these are three separate testimonies,
but they are one testimony for הזמה.
It turns out that a zomem witness pays money
through the testimony of his brother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רבא: וליטעמיך, הא דתנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic offered in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's logic that a pair of relatives is invalid because one's הזמה depends on the other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה of three brothers, one brother's payment as a זומם depends on his brothers also being proven false, yet the testimony is accepted. So that kind of dependence does not make testimony invalid.

steps.title: Exposing a false witness comes from outside witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that in the three-brothers case, הזמה comes from the outside witnesses. The same is true for any pair of relatives, so רמי בר חמא's logic falls apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the exposure (הזמה) comes from other people. Here too, the exposure comes from other people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the three-brothers case is allowed. He then uses the same reason to knock down רמי בר חמא's logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness becomes a זומם only because outside witnesses say he was with them somewhere else. They are the cause of his punishment, not his brother. Since the same is true for two relatives testifying together, there is no logical reason left to disqualify them.

keyTerms.meaning: Proving witnesses false by showing they were somewhere else at the time
From the outside world, meaning from other people

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is saying relatives may testify together. He is only rejecting this logical proof. The rule itself stays, and the next step gives a פסוק for it.

phrases.english: Rather, the exposure as false witnesses comes from others.
Here too, the exposure comes from others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's challenge from step 7 and uses it to reject רמי בר חמא's reasoning.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רמי בר חמא's logical source from step 6 that relatives cannot form a pair of witnesses.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The punishment of a זומם is caused by the outside witnesses who expose him, not by his relative's testimony.

steps.title: A new source from the plural word 'and children'
steps.stepSummary: With the logic gone, the גמרא learns the rule from the פסוק. The plural 'ובנים' teaches that related children cannot testify together even about an outsider.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if so, the פסוק should have written 'and a son for fathers' or 'they for fathers.' Why does it say 'and children'? To teach that children are disqualified even about other people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question from step 5, this time from the words of the פסוק instead of from logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have used a singular word ('ובן') or a pronoun ('הם'). The extra plural 'ובנים' pictures several relatives testifying together. That teaches that relatives cannot be a pair of witnesses even when the case is about an outsider ('לעלמא').

keyTerms.meaning: Let the פסוק write (it could have said it differently)
About other people in general, outsiders

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the rule that two relatives cannot join as a pair of witnesses about anyone.

phrases.english: Rather, if so,
let the verse write 'and a son for fathers,'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:16

phrases.english: or else 'they for fathers.'
What does 'and children' come to teach?
Even children testifying together about others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the logical source that was just rejected with a source from the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra plural 'ובנים' teaches that relatives may not testify together even about an outsider.

steps.title: What is the source for relatives from the mother's side?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק speaks about fathers and sons, so it covers the father's relatives. The גמרא asks for a source for the mother's relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for relatives on the father's side. Where do we learn relatives on the mother's side?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. It is setting up the next step, which will give a source for the mother's relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything learned so far comes from words like 'אבות' and 'בנים', which point to the father's family. The mother's family is not clearly included, so a separate source is needed.

phrases.english: We have found a source for the father's relatives;
from where do we know the mother's relatives?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן קְרוֹבֵי הָאָב, קְרוֹבֵי הָאֵם מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the source just found and asks whether it reaches the mother's relatives too.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that relatives on the mother's side are also disqualified as witnesses.

steps.title: The repeated word 'fathers' covers the mother's relatives
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אבות' appears twice in the פסוק. The extra one is not needed for the father's relatives, so it teaches the mother's relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'fathers' and 'fathers', twice. If the extra one is not needed for the father's relatives, apply it to the mother's relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 10 by pointing to a word that the פסוק repeats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's relatives are already taught by one 'אבות'. A second 'אבות' would add nothing for them. Using the rule 'אם אינו ענין', the extra word is applied to the mother's relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this matter (so apply it to another)

phrases.english: The verse says 'fathers', 'fathers': two times.
phrases.notes: דברים 24:16 says 'fathers' at the start and again in 'for fathers'.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of the father's relatives,
apply it to the matter of the mother's relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the mother's relatives.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second, extra 'אבות' teaches that the mother's relatives are disqualified too.
steps.whatToRemember: Father's relatives come from the main words of the פסוק. Mother's relatives come from the extra 'אבות'.

steps.title: What about testimony that helps a relative?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק talks about being 'put to death', which is testimony that hurts the relative. The גמרא asks for a source that a relative cannot testify in his favor either.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found that a relative cannot testify against him. From where do we know he cannot testify for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It is setting up the next move, which will give a source for testimony that helps a relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא יומתו' ('shall not be put to death') describe testimony that harms the relative. That does not clearly cover testimony that helps him, so a separate source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: In his favor, to his benefit

phrases.english: We have found a source for testimony against him;
phrases.notes: This comes from 'shall not be put to death' in the same פסוק, which is testimony that hurts.

phrases.english: from where do we know testimony in his favor?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After covering which relatives are disqualified, the גמרא asks about the type of testimony: testimony that helps the relative.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that relatives cannot testify in each other's favor.

steps.title: The double 'יומתו' teaches that relatives cannot testify in each other's favor
steps.stepSummary: The word 'יומתו' appears twice in the פסוק. One is enough to forbid testimony that hurts a relative, so the extra one forbids testimony that helps him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'יומתו' two times. If the second one is not needed to teach about testimony against a relative, use it to teach about testimony in his favor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12. It finds a source that a relative may not testify in his relative's favor either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony against a relative is already forbidden by one 'יומתו'. The second one would add nothing there. Using the rule of אם אינו ענין, the גמרא moves that extra word over to testimony that helps the relative.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall be put to death (the word repeated in the פסוק)
If it is not needed for this matter, apply it to another one
To someone's benefit (testimony in his favor)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why a relative is disqualified completely, whether his testimony would help his relative or hurt him.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'shall be put to death,' 'shall be put to death'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:16: 'לא יומתו אבות על בנים ובנים לא יומתו על אבות.'

phrases.english: two times.
If it is not needed for the matter of testimony to his harm,
apply it to the matter of testimony to his benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: יוּמְתוּ יוּמְתוּ תְּרֵי זִימְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second, extra 'יומתו' teaches that a relative cannot testify in his relative's favor.

steps.title: Source needed for money cases
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק talks about the death penalty, so it covers דיני נפשות. The גמרא asks where we learn the same rule for דיני ממונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found the rule for cases of capital law. For cases of monetary law, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. The source so far covers only death-penalty cases, and it wants a source for money cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יומתו' is about execution. So everything learned up to now is limited to דיני נפשות. The גמרא needs something to extend the rule to ordinary money cases.

phrases.english: We have found it in cases of capital law,
in cases of monetary law, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן בְּדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת, בְּדִינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to extend the source just completed to a new area of law
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that relatives are disqualified in monetary cases too

steps.title: 'משפט אחד' makes money cases follow the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'משפט אחד יהיה לכם' teaches that the law should be the same for you. So money cases follow the rules of capital cases here.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'You shall have one law.' This means a law that is the same for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 14 with a פסוק. 'One law' means דיני ממונות and דיני נפשות share this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'משפט אחד' is read as 'one equal law' for all kinds of cases. So the disqualification of relatives learned for דיני נפשות carries over to דיני ממונות.

keyTerms.meaning: A law that is equal (the same for all cases)

steps.whatToRemember: Relatives are disqualified completely: testimony for or against, in capital cases and in money cases. The sources are 'ובנים' (step 9), the extra 'אבות' (step 11), the double 'יומתו', and 'משפט אחד'.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'You shall have one law'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:22

phrases.english: meaning: a law that is the same for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: מִשְׁפַּט אֶחָד יִהְיֶה לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'משפט אחד' teaches that money cases are equal to capital cases for this rule.

steps.title: רב: my uncle's family and my family cannot testify about each other
steps.stepSummary: רב says his father's brother, along with that uncle's son and son-in-law, cannot testify about him. In the same way, רב, his son and his son-in-law cannot testify about the uncle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: My father's brother may not testify about me, not he, not his son, and not his son-in-law. And also I may not testify about him, not I, not my son, and not my son-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section starts. רב gives a practical statement about which relatives are disqualified, using his own uncle as the example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists relatives like a father's brother, his son and his son-in-law. רב adds that this works in both directions. Just as the uncle's side cannot testify about רב, רב's side cannot testify about the uncle.
steps.confusionAlert: 'לא יעיד לי' does not only mean 'testify for me'. Based on step 13, it covers testimony that helps or hurts.

phrases.english: Rav said:
My father's brother will not testify about me,
not he, nor his son, nor his son-in-law.
Likewise, I will not testify about him,
not I, nor my son, nor my son-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אֲחִי אַבָּא לֹא יָעִיד לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from finding the source to applying the rule to specific relatives
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disqualification goes both ways: the uncle, his son and son-in-law cannot testify about the nephew, and the nephew, his son and son-in-law cannot testify about the uncle.

steps.title: Why is רב's son disqualified? The משנה doesn't list third-with-first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's statement. His son testifying about רב's uncle is 'third generation with first,' and the משנה only lists 'second with second' and 'second with first.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why should that be? This is a third-generation relative testifying about a first-generation relative. We learned in the משנה about second with second, and about second with first, but we never learned about third with first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last part of רב's statement, where he said his son cannot testify about his uncle. It says the משנה never disqualifies that level of relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Count the generations from the two brothers, רב's father and his uncle, who are the first generation. רב and his cousin are the second generation, and רב's son is the third. The משנה lists a cousin (second with second) and a nephew (second with first), but it does not list a grand-nephew (third with first), so where does רב get that one from?

keyTerms.meaning: Why? (a challenge, asking for the reason)
Third generation with first generation, like a grand-nephew and his great-uncle
Second generation with second generation, like two cousins
Second generation with first generation, like a nephew and his uncle

steps.confusionAlert: The 'generations' are counted from the two brothers (רב's father and his uncle) as the first generation, not from רב himself.

phrases.english: And why?
phrases.notes: He means: why can רב's son not testify about רב's uncle, as רב just said in the last step?

phrases.english: It is third generation with first generation,
and we learned second with second,
we learned second with first,
but third with first we did not learn!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the final clause of רב's statement in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that his son cannot testify about his father's brother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists only second-with-second and second-with-first relatives. Third-with-first is never mentioned, so there seems to be no source for disqualifying it.

steps.title: The משנה's 'son-in-law' means the son's son-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word 'his son-in-law' in the משנה means 'his son's son-in-law,' which is a third-generation relative. So third-with-first is in the משנה after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'his son-in-law,' which is taught in our משנה, mean? It means the son-in-law of his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by re-reading one word in the משנה. 'His son-in-law' really refers to a third-generation relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the relatives themselves, their sons, and their sons-in-law are disqualified. If 'son-in-law' means the uncle's son's son-in-law, that is the husband of a granddaughter, who is in the third generation. So the משנה does include third-with-first, and רב's ruling has a source.

keyTerms.meaning: His son-in-law (the word in the משנה)
The son-in-law of his son, meaning the husband of his granddaughter

phrases.english: What is 'his son-in-law'
that is taught in our משנה?
The son-in-law of his son.
phrases.notes: That's the husband of his granddaughter, so he is a third-generation relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'His son-in-law' means a direct son-in-law, which is only second generation, so third-with-first is not in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'His son-in-law' means the son's son-in-law, a third-generation relative, so the משנה does cover third-with-first.

steps.title: Then why not just say 'his son's son'?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה wanted to teach about the third generation, it could have said 'his son's son,' which is simpler.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let the משנה say 'his son's son'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. If the משנה meant a third-generation relative, why did it pick the roundabout phrase 'son-in-law'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A grandson is the most obvious third-generation relative. Choosing 'son-in-law' to hint at the son's son-in-law seems like a strange way to teach the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But let it teach (a challenge suggesting better wording)

phrases.english: But let it teach 'his son's son'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'his son-in-law' as 'his son's son-in-law'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה wanted a third-generation example, 'his son's son' would be clearer, so why use 'son-in-law'?

steps.title: A side lesson: a husband counts like his wife
steps.stepSummary: The משנה chose 'son-in-law' to teach a side lesson in passing: a husband is treated exactly like his wife for relationships.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is teaching us a point in passing: a husband is like his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה used 'son-in-law' instead of 'grandson.' The wording teaches an extra rule along the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By using the granddaughter's husband as its example, the משנה shows that a husband stands in his wife's place. He is related to her family at the same level she is. So a son-in-law is treated just like a son, and the son's son-in-law just like the son's son.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband is like his wife (he takes her place in family relationships)

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the גמרא reads the משנה's 'חתנו' as 'his son's son-in-law,' and says the משנה chose that wording to teach בעל כאשתו. Step 21 challenges this reading, and step 22 drops it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'בעל כאשתו' means that relatives by marriage are disqualified at the same levels as blood relatives.

phrases.english: A matter in passing
it teaches us,
that a husband is like his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording teaches an extra lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Son-in-law' is a needlessly roundabout way to say grandson.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording deliberately teaches that a husband is like his wife, so in-laws are equal to blood relatives.

steps.title: רבי חייא's count of twenty-four does not fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught that there are eight main relatives, which make twenty-four in total. If the משנה also included a grandson-level relative, the total would be thirty-two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about רבי חייא's teaching: eight 'fathers,' which are twenty-four? According to you, they would be thirty-two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 18, which said 'his son-in-law' really means 'his son's son-in-law.' It brings a ברייתא whose numbers do not work with that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא counts eight main relatives. Each one comes with a son and a son-in-law, so 8 × 3 = 24. If the משנה also meant a third-generation relative (the son's son-in-law), each of the eight would have four people, making 32, not 24.

keyTerms.meaning: Eight 'fathers': the eight main relatives listed in the משנה

phrases.english: But then, what about that which רבי חייא teaches:
Eight 'fathers,'
phrases.notes: These are the eight main relatives the משנה lists as unable to testify.

phrases.english: which are twenty-four.
phrases.notes: Each relative comes with his son and his son-in-law: 8 × 3 = 24.

phrases.english: According to you, these would be thirty-two!
phrases.notes: Add a grandson-level relative to each one and you get 8 × 4 = 32.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading 'his son's son-in-law' from Step 18, which Step 20 had defended.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'חתנו' in the משנה as 'his son's son-in-law.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא's numbers count only son and son-in-law for each relative (24). Adding a third-generation relative would give 32, so the משנה cannot be including that generation.

steps.title: It means his actual son-in-law, who counts as another generation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back and says 'his son-in-law' means his real son-in-law. It was called 'his son's son-in-law' because a son-in-law comes from outside the family and is treated like one generation lower.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really means his actual son-in-law. And why did we call him 'his son's son-in-law'? Since he comes from outside the family, he is like another generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'son's son-in-law' reading and keeps the plain meaning, 'actual son-in-law.' It still tries to support רב by saying a son-in-law counts as a lower generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the count of 24 works, since there is no extra relative. To keep רב's ruling inside the משנה, the גמרא argues that a son-in-law is one step further away than a son because he married in from outside. That would let him stand for a third-generation relative.

phrases.english: Rather, it really means his actual son-in-law.
And why did we call him 'his son's son-in-law'?
phrases.notes: This is the name used in Step 18 to support רב's ruling.

phrases.english: Since he comes from outside the family,
he is like another generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by going back to the plain meaning of 'his son-in-law.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: plain meaning restored, with the son-in-law treated as a lower generation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'His son-in-law' meant a third-generation relative (the son's son-in-law), which would break רבי חייא's count.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is the actual son-in-law. Because he comes from outside the family, he counts as one generation lower.

steps.title: Then it is third with second, which רב allows
steps.stepSummary: If the son-in-law counts as one generation lower, the משנה's case becomes 'third with second.' But רב holds that third with second may testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is third with second, and רב allows third with second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in Step 22. Treating the son-in-law as one generation lower creates a new problem for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a son-in-law counts as one generation lower, then the משנה, by disqualifying the son-in-law, is disqualifying a 'third with second' case. But רב is known to allow third with second. So this reading would make the משנה contradict רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A third-generation relative testifying about a second-generation relative
He declared it valid (allowed the testimony)

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, הָוֵה לֵיהּ שְׁלִישִׁי בְּשֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: If so, it is third with second,
phrases.notes: Counting the son-in-law one step lower turns the משנה's son-in-law case into 'third with second.'

phrases.english: and רב allows third with second.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הָוֵה לֵיהּ שְׁלִישִׁי בְּשֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 22's idea that the son-in-law is 'another generation.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a son-in-law counts as a lower generation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Then the משנה's disqualification of the son-in-law would be a disqualification of 'third with second,' yet רב allows third with second. So the משנה would contradict רב.

steps.title: רב follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב's ruling does not come from the משנה. It comes from רבי אלעזר, who disqualifies the uncle's son with his son and son-in-law, just like the uncle himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב said this following רבי אלעזר. As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי אלעזר says, just as my father's brother may not testify for me (he, his son and his son-in-law), so too my father's brother's son may not testify for me (he, his son and his son-in-law).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops trying to fit רב into the משנה. It says רב is following a different תנא, רבי אלעזר, and quotes his ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר disqualifies more relatives than the משנה. The uncle's son is also disqualified together with his own son and son-in-law, the same way the uncle is. רב's ruling about a third generation fits this wider view, but the next step challenges this answer, and step 26 refines it.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא could not find רב's 'third with first' ruling in the משנה, so it says רב follows רבי אלעזר, who disqualifies more relatives than the משנה. Step 26 refines this: רב agrees with רבי אלעזר on only one point.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא proved the משנה includes third with first. The final answer is that רב is NOT following the משנה here but a different תנא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: when a אמורא's ruling cannot be read into the משנה, the גמרא finds a ברייתא with a different תנא that he follows.

phrases.english: Rather, רב said this following רבי אלעזר.
As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי אלעזר says,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֲחִי אַבָּא לֹא יָעִיד לִי –
phrases.english: Just as my father's brother may not testify for me,
not he, his son or his son-in-law,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ בֶּן אֲחִי אַבָּא לֹא יָעִיד לִי –
phrases.english: so too, my father's brother's son may not testify for me,
not he, his son or his son-in-law.
phrases.notes: This is the extra step beyond the משנה: the cousin's family line is disqualified too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23, and the challenge from Step 17, by proposing a different source for רב. Step 25 then challenges this answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different תנא: רב follows a ברייתא rather than the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's disqualification of his son testifying about his uncle (third with first) is based on רבי אלעזר, who disqualifies more relatives than the משנה.

steps.title: But רבי אלעזר still disqualifies third with second
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רב follows רבי אלעזר. Under רבי אלעזר's view there is still a case of 'third with second' that is disqualified, and רב allows that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, there is a case of 'third with second' here, and רב allows 'third with second' to testify!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 24. If רב's ruling comes from רבי אלעזר, how can רב allow 'third with second' when רבי אלעזר's case includes one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24 the problem was moved from the משנה over to רבי אלעזר. But רבי אלעזר also disqualifies a relative who is 'third with second.' So the same contradiction with רב comes back, now aimed at רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: But still. The problem has not gone away.
A relative from the third generation testifying about one from the second generation
He declared fit, meaning allowed to testify

steps.confusionAlert: This sounds like a repeat of step 23, but it is a new challenge. Step 23 was aimed at the משנה. This one is aimed at רבי אלעזר, whom step 24 brought in as רב's source.

phrases.english: But still, it is a case of third with second,
phrases.notes: He means within רבי אלעזר's case from the last step, where a third-generation relative is disqualified about a second-generation one.

phrases.english: and רב allows third with second!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 24 by showing that רבי אלעזר's view still clashes with רב
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב's ruling is based on רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר disqualifies a third-generation relative about a second-generation one, but רב explicitly allows third with second, so רב cannot simply be following רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: רב agrees with רבי אלעזר on one point and disagrees on another
steps.stepSummary: רב follows רבי אלעזר only partly. He agrees that a third-generation relative is disqualified about a first-generation one, but he disagrees about third with second.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב agrees with him on one thing and disagrees with him on one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב never claimed to follow רבי אלעזר completely. He takes one rule from him and rejects the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point they share is that a third-generation relative is disqualified about a first-generation relative (שלישי בראשון). The point they argue about is third with second: רבי אלעזר disqualifies it and רב allows it. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like him, meaning he agrees
In one thing, on one point

phrases.english: רב agrees with him in one thing,
phrases.notes: The one thing is that third with first is disqualified.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him in one thing.
phrases.notes: The other thing is third with second. רב allows it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial agreement: the source is followed on one rule but not on the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב must follow רבי אלעזר in everything
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי אלעזר on third with first, but rejects his ruling on third with second

steps.title: What is רב's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רב uses for disqualifying an extra generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רב's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רב learns his view from. This sets up the next step, where the answer will come from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know רב disqualifies third with first but not third with second, the גמרא wants the source that gives him exactly that much and no more.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?

phrases.english: What is the reason of רב?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling רב's position, the גמרא asks for its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for רב's view

steps.title: רב learns one extra generation from 'and children'
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'and children' (ובנים) in the פסוק includes one more generation, the grandchildren. That gives third with first, but nothing beyond it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says, 'Fathers shall not be put to death for children, and children,' this comes to include another generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב learns from the extra word 'and children' (ובנים) that one more generation is disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and children' add exactly one more generation, so the grandchildren are disqualified too. This covers third with first. Because the פסוק only adds one generation in this way, רב does not stretch it to cover third with second.

keyTerms.meaning: Fathers shall not be put to death for children (דברים 24:16). It is read as a source for relatives not testifying.

phrases.english: As the verse says:
'Fathers shall not be put to death for children, and children,'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:16. The extra word 'and children' is the key.

phrases.english: to include another generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'ובנים' adds exactly one more generation, which gives third with first.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: whoever is disqualified about a father is disqualified about his children
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads 'על בנים' as a rule: any relative who is disqualified from testifying about a father is also disqualified about that father's children. That is how he reaches third with second.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר says: the תורה said 'על בנים.' Those disqualified about the fathers are thrown onto the children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבי אלעזר's source from the same פסוק. He reads it in a way that reaches further than רב does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר does not just add one generation. He makes a general rule that every disqualification about a father passes down to that father's children. That is why he also disqualifies third with second, which רב allows.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Those who are disqualified about the fathers
Onto the children (אַ = on, plus בָּנִים)

steps.whatToRemember: רב and רבי אלעזר both use the same פסוק. רב reads 'ובנים' as adding one generation, so he disqualifies third with first only. רבי אלעזר reads 'על בנים' as a general rule that every disqualification about a father passes to his children, so he also disqualifies third with second.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the exact limits of רב's ruling, that third with second may testify. It also shows that the argument between them comes from two different ways of reading one פסוק.

phrases.english: And רבי אלעזר says:
The Torah said 'for children':
those disqualified about the fathers, throw them onto the children.
phrases.notes: אַבָּנִים here is short for 'on the children.' Anyone who can't testify about a father also can't testify about his kids.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, עַל בָּנִים אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אלעזר's reading of the same פסוק, as a contrast to רב's reading in step 28
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר reads 'על בנים' as a general rule that every disqualification about a father passes to his children, which includes third with second.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב adds only one generation from 'ובנים', while רבי אלעזר passes every disqualification down from fathers to children, so he also disqualifies third with second.

steps.title: רב נחמן's three in-law relatives who may not testify
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that his mother-in-law's brother, her brother's son, and her sister's son may not testify for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: My mother-in-law's brother may not testify for me. My mother-in-law's brother's son may not testify for me. My mother-in-law's sister's son may not testify for me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives three practical cases of relatives through his wife's mother who are not allowed to be witnesses for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three people are related to him only through marriage, through his wife's mother. He is saying this link is close enough to disqualify them. The next step shows the משנה already says this, if you look at it from the other side.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
My mother-in-law's brother may not testify for me;

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן אֲחִי חֲמוֹתִי לֹא יָעִיד לִי,
phrases.english: the son of my mother-in-law's brother may not testify for me;

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן אֲחוֹת חֲמוֹתִי לֹא יָעִיד לִי.
phrases.english: the son of my mother-in-law's sister may not testify for me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the generation-counting debate to specific in-law cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The brother of one's mother-in-law, and the sons of her brother and her sister, are disqualified from testifying for him.

steps.title: The משנה already teaches רב נחמן's cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the משנה's list (sister's husband, father's sister's husband, mother's sister's husband, with their sons and sons-in-law) covers רב נחמן's three cases from the other side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our משנה also taught this: his sister's husband, his father's sister's husband, and his mother's sister's husband, they themselves, their sons, and their sons-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב נחמן by quoting the משנה, which teaches the same thing in different words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Look at it from the witness's side. To his mother-in-law's brother, רב נחמן is the son-in-law of that man's sister's husband: 'בעל אחותו... וחתניהן'. To her brother's son, he is the son-in-law of that man's father's sister's husband. To her sister's son, he is the son-in-law of that man's mother's sister's husband. Since the link works both ways, the משנה's list proves רב נחמן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: and our תנא (the משנה) also taught it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the words 'mother-in-law' in the משנה. It describes the same family link from the other person's side, through the word 'וחתניהן' (their sons-in-law).

phrases.english: And our tanna also taught it:
phrases.notes: 'Our tanna' means our משנה.

phrases.english: his sister's husband,
and his father's sister's husband,
and his mother's sister's husband,
they, and their sons, and their sons-in-law.
phrases.notes: The key word is 'their sons-in-law'. That son-in-law is רב נחמן in each of his three cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's ruling from the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's list of sisters' husbands, with their sons and sons-in-law, read from the other relative's side.

steps.title: The question in עולא's study hall about a father-in-law's relatives
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that in עולא's study hall they asked about the father-in-law's brother, his brother's son, and his sister's son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When we were in עולא's study hall, we asked: What is the law for one's father-in-law's brother? For the son of his father-in-law's brother? For the son of his father-in-law's sister?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tells of a question about the same kind of cases, but through the wife's father instead of her mother. This sets up עולא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors רב נחמן's list exactly, only switching mother-in-law to father-in-law. The question is whether these men may testify for him or are disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: when we were in עולא's study hall
we asked / it was a question for us

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When we were in Ulla's study hall,
we asked:
His father-in-law's brother, what is the law?
The son of his father-in-law's brother, what is the law?
The son of his father-in-law's sister, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the father-in-law version of רב נחמן's mother-in-law cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the father-in-law's brother, and the sons of his brother and sister, are disqualified as witnesses.

steps.title: עולא: the משנה already answers this
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the משנה's list of brother, father's brother, and mother's brother, with their sons and sons-in-law, already covers these cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to us: You already learned it in the משנה: his brother, his father's brother, and his mother's brother, they, their sons, and their sons-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question by pointing to the משנה. All three relatives are disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, flip the view. To the father-in-law's brother, the man is his brother's son-in-law: 'אחיו... וחתניהן'. To the father-in-law's brother's son, he is the son-in-law of that man's father's brother. To the father-in-law's sister's son, he is the son-in-law of that man's mother's brother. So all three are already listed in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: you already learned it (in the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Family links that disqualify witnesses work both ways. Many in-law cases are already in the משנה if you read the list from the other relative's side, especially through the word 'וחתניהן' (their sons-in-law).

phrases.english: He said to us: You already learned it:
his brother, and his father's brother, and his mother's brother,
they, and their sons, and their sons-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from עולא's study hall.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All three are disqualified. The משנה's list of brothers and uncles, with their sons-in-law, covers them when read from the other side.

steps.title: A story begins: רב came to buy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a story about רב, who arrived somewhere to buy something.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב happened to come to a place to buy...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new story about רב. This line only sets the scene, and the story continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet. This line only opens a story about רב, and the story continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav happened to come to buy

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story after the in-law discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. It is the opening of a story about רב.
